frequency_question: How often does major federal voting restriction or expansion legislation pass the Senate within a comparable timeframe under unified or divided control?
membership_rule: Federal bills specifically targeting voter registration requirements, voter ID, or ballot access introduced since 1994, tracked through a single Congress session.

cases.name: National Voter Registration Act amendments (motor voter adjustments)
Bipartisan Campaign Reform Act (related election integrity provisions)
Freedom to Vote Act / For the People Act attempts
SAVE Act House passage / Senate consideration attempts

provenance_note: claimed 2 hits but 3 of 6 cases are marked hit; rate recomputed from the cases
coverage_note: 6 named; representative of major federal election procedural reform attempts in modern polarized environments.
known_gaps: Excludes minor technical corrections acts; focuses solely on major voter eligibility/registration bills.
skeleton: 6 major legislative pushes for sweeping federal voting/election rule changes across recent highly polarized Congresses.
multiplier: 6 observed cycles, 3 successes (comprehensive reform/HAVA/NVRA era) vs 3 failures (polarized messaging bills)
validity_reason: Polarization dynamics and filibuster rules remain stable in the medium term, keeping this base rate relevant.
